source: IRS IR-2025-103 (Oct 9 2025) and Rev. Proc. 2025-32 (IRB 2025-45). Single and married-joint brackets, all four standard deductions read verbatim from the release; head-of-household and separate brackets and all capital-gains thresholds read from the bulletin summary. Amounts in cents. Checked Nov 2026.
notes: Brackets and the standard deduction are treated as indexed to inflation, so in the simulation's today's dollars they stay constant. The Social Security taxation thresholds are not indexed by law. IRMAA tiers are indexed; each tier row is [upper MAGI edge, extra monthly Part B surcharge in cents]. Not modeled: the extra deduction for age 65+, the senior deduction, the net investment income tax, Part D surcharges, state rules.

irmaa.source: Part B tiers from SSA POMS HI 01101.020 (effective 12/02/2025, MAGI from 2024 returns) and the $202.90 standard premium on medicare.gov; the CMS fact sheet could not be read, so the tiers are not cross-checked against CMS. Surcharge is the tier's total Part B premium minus $202.90. Part D surcharges are not included. Edges are inclusive upper limits in cents; the top-but-one tier ends one cent short of the 'or more' line.

payroll.source: SSA contribution and benefit base, 2026: $184,500 (https://www.ssa.gov/oact/cola/cbb.html). Employee rates: 6.2% Social Security, 1.45% Medicare; the additional Medicare tax is not modeled.

seniors.source: Additional standard deduction for age 65 and over: Rev. Proc. 2025-32 section 4.14(3), read in IRB 2025-45. Extra senior deduction: IRS 'Working Families Tax Cuts: Tax deductions for working Americans and seniors' ($6,000 per person aged 65 or more by year end, tax years 2025 through 2028, married couples must file jointly, phases out above $75,000 of modified AGI or $150,000 joint). The 6% phase-out rate is from the statute (P.L. 119-21 section 70103); the IRS page read gives the thresholds only. Amounts in cents.
